meta.title: Stepwise runs — one step, one run, one verdict
meta.description: 0.6 LABRIG source: detached admission, plan-bound supervisor state, validated checks and revision ordering, one-prefix UI projection. Bundled Planner 1.5.0 requires matching deployment. Prior happy-path benchmarks remain historical evidence, not full lifecycle proof. See release-0.6-LABRIG.md and loop-contract.

frames.label: 2 · Drive — the new part: who decides what runs next
3 · Run — one step, start to verdict

nodes.label: The user's prompt
nodes.note: Used ONCE, to plan — and, after 2026-09-04, only after the model has read the code the task is about. Never re-injected per step: re-injecting it into every iteration is what let one run wander across the whole task.

nodes.label: Plan gate
nodes.sublabel: read first (bounded), then a FORCED commit_plan · hands off to the supervisor
nodes.note: Bounded planning requires structured commit_plan with executable criteria; malformed/missing plans suspend, no prose execution fallback. Answer-only uses same runner.

nodes.label: Step criteria
nodes.sublabel: each step declares a check that CAN FAIL · constants and script paths rejected
nodes.note:
commit_plan gains a `verify` field per step, validated at commit time. Three runnable forms: a check_page eval returning a boolean, a command judged by exit code, a file that must contain a named symbol. Existence-only checks are rejected.

The first live attempt (improve-forced) wrote expr "true" on every step, pointed at .js files — a constant cannot fail and check_page cannot render a script. Both are now rejected with an error that names the fix, and the forced retry carries it.

Answered live on the next run: `contains js/config.js "MAX_SPEED"`, `contains js/physics.js "class CarPhysics"`, and for the final step an eval on the served URL checking the canvas and both HUD elements. The model writes usable checks when the shape is constrained and the call is forced.

nodes.label: plan event
nodes.note: Immutable plan event identity and full plan.state snapshots; latest-plan reducer never inherits older indexed checkpoints.

nodes.label: Step supervisor
nodes.sublabel: owns the cursor · an autopilot turn with an unfinished plan RESUMES it
nodes.note: Persists attempt/revision/pair counters and selection cursor. All entry points use shared supervisor and safe control boundaries.

nodes.label: Step prompt writer
nodes.sublabel: the prompt for ONE step · its check verbatim · the SOURCE the plan was made from
nodes.note:
Assembled from committed facts rather than generated prose, so the prompt cannot drift from the plan it claims to execute. It carries the step, its files, its check quoted verbatim, only the steps already VERIFIED as context — and, since 2026-09-04, the source the model read while planning.

A step starts with a fresh window. Without the planning reads the model had never seen the file it was told to split: it re-read all 435 lines, which alone spent the four iterations it had, and never reached a write — no writes at all in two attempts (improve-overrun). The reads that informed the plan now ride into every step as a tool-result item, capped at 40k chars, with the instruction not to re-read.

The user's original prompt is used once, to plan, and never re-injected.

nodes.label: Revision decider
nodes.sublabel: reopen an earlier step as rev_n · cap 2 · re-verify downstream
nodes.note: Structured request_revision, invalidate dependent evidence BEFORE editing, target correction/verification then downstream checks. Selected scope suspends for out-of-scope repair.

nodes.label: Step run
nodes.sublabel: one step · SESSION registry · THINK level honoured · a retry is TOLD why it failed · earns iterations while it changes files · judged by its check
nodes.note: A retry used to start blind: the prompt was the same, the model never saw the failed verdict, and the step it re-did was the one that had just failed (NFQ step 4, a Three.js TypeError, 2026-09-05). Now the step prompt carries the failed check and what was observed, first thing. The iteration cap is not fixed either: a step earns another window while the workspace fingerprint keeps moving (guard-based extension); a step that stops changing files stops.

nodes.label: Step verify
nodes.sublabel: run the step's own check · pass / fail, with evidence · fails CLOSED · session registry
nodes.note:
Runs what the step declared: the eval, the command, the file check. The verdict is an observation, not the model's opinion that it is finished.

Every kind fails CLOSED. A check that cannot run is exactly as unproven as one that failed, and treating "could not check" as success is how a plan goes green while nothing works — the car run's check_page returned "eval produced no result" and that now reads as a failure.

nodes.label: checkpoint event
nodes.sublabel: step N, rev R — verdict, the check, its evidence, and why
nodes.note: Canonical plan.state saved before projection-only compatibility checkpoint; interrupted process never manufactures a settled check.

nodes.label: events.jsonl
nodes.sublabel: one log · plan, runs, checkpoints, revisions

nodes.label: GET /report + /state
nodes.sublabel: GET /report + /state — status from checkpoints · /state carries the working log per reply
nodes.note: Report and plan are from the same replay projection; no filesystem-based passed status. 0.6 /state packages both with one cursor.

nodes.label: Native plan strip
nodes.sublabel: SIMPLE surface · steps, which is running, pass/fail · no knobs
nodes.note: Reads canonical report inside /state, retains completed plan; snapshot includes activephase. Real Go API desktop/mobile pause/reload/reconnect verification passed; prod0.5unchanged.

nodes.label: RFX Planner panel
nodes.sublabel: ADVANCED surface · calls runStep(), no longer writes prompts
nodes.note: Repo Planner1.5.0 built withserver-owned whole/selected scope andcanonicalpendingstates. Noautomaticbrowserrestarts. Host+pack not installed; deployment remains open.

ports.shape: POST run-step {step, rev?} · POST auto {on} · GET plan-state

nodes.label: Step control API
nodes.sublabel: GET /plan · POST /plan/step — the one way to drive a plan
nodes.note: POSTcommands accepts chat/step/continue/selected withpersistedcommandIDs; controls matchrun/controlversion. Legacy HTTPwaiters observe detachedworker.

same state, richer rendering
